chapter: Decca years and the First Herd
title: Women instrumentalists and new colors: vibes, guitar, Ralph Burns
summary: He hired trumpeter Billie Rogers and vibraphonist Marjorie Hyams, and sought new colors like vibes, clarinet and guitar that Ralph Burns wrote for.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: You were one of the first -- if not most of it -- people who had started to use female instrumentalists. You had Billie Rogers on trumpet.

Yeah, she was first with the band. That would be about '41, I think. And then later, in '44, I hired Hyams, Marjorie Hines, a very good vibra-harpist. As a matter of fact, she was there and then she was followed by Red Norvo, so she wound up in very good class. And when she left the band, she went with George Shearing's first sextet.
What was your feeling about incorporating the vibes and other instruments? You've had different instruments, because you had the guitar --

Well, I was constantly seeking other colors, you know, as to what it could be and still be able to get a good swinging thing going. And that's why in those years I guess we were starting to use the sound of vibes, clarinet, guitar and piano. And Ralph had the great ability of writing for these odd instrumentations and -- odd at the time -- and making it happen, especially against the big band.
